💬 Iran marks 40 days since funeral ceremony of martyred Leader

📌 Tehran, IRNA – A commemorative ceremony for the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei and his family hss begun at Imam Khomeini Musalla in Tehran on the 40th day after a historic funeral procession across the country.

The ceremony was held on Tuesday afternoon at the invitation of the current Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei.
​
It was attended by Ayatollah Seyyed Hassan Khomeini, grandson of founder of the Islamic Republic Imam Khomeini, Hojjatoleslam Masoud Khamenei and Hojjatoleslam Mostafa Khamenei, the surviving family members of the martyred Leader.
​
Also, the First Vice President Mohammad-Reza Aref, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Judiciary Chief Hojjatoleslam Gholamhossein Mohseni-Ejei, as well as governmental and military officials and a large crowd of admirers of the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution attended the ceremony.

Netanyahu, Kushner, and the Board of Peace

Jared Kushner arrived in Jerusalem after sitting in Cairo with Egyptian, Qatari and Turkish mediators, in meetings that included Hamas representatives. Then came more than four hours with Benjamin Netanyahu, a prime minister who had called the new Gaza roadmap “unacceptable” only days earlier.

Netanyahu brought Shin Bet chief David Zini and military-intelligence chief Shlomi Binder. Israel’s message was that Hamas had violated its commitments and that Turkish funding remained part of the problem. 

The American delegation included Kushner, Gaza Board of Peace director-general Nickolay Mladenov, Tony Blair and senior advisers. 

The agreement, in the Israeli telling, is simple. No reconstruction before Hamas is fully disarmed. No further Israeli redeployment before Gaza is demilitarized. 

Every rifle, rocket, tunnel and workshop must become an item in a supervised disposal process. Israel will retain what it calls the right to self-defense and to act against any renewed Hamas activity. 

Then comes the public-health track.
The Prime Minister’s Office said the sides created two working groups. One will handle Hamas’s disarmament and Gaza’s demilitarization. The other will address sanitation, clean water and public health, including issues that “also impact the people of Israel.” Gaza’s future has been divided into two tasks: remove the weapons, then contain the disease. 

The mechanics of disarmament changed during the day. Early reports said Hamas would hand weapons to an American force for destruction. 

Later accounts said Hamas would first transfer them to a Palestinian technocratic government, which would then pass them to an International Stabilization Force. One thing did not change: an American general would supervise and verify the process. 

The underlying dispute did not disappear. Netanyahu insists targeted killings will continue while Hamas remains armed. Kushner reportedly wants Israel to take limited steps that could test whether Hamas’s disarmament pledge is genuine, while the U.S. works to prevent a wider escalation. 

They agreed to build a “deconfliction” mechanism, diplomacy’s way of admitting that the deal is being negotiated under live fire. 

Smotrich said the quiet part out loud. Israel’s goal of destroying Hamas, he argued, is incompatible with negotiating with Hamas leaders who “should not be alive at all.” 

That is the whole roadmap in one sentence. Hamas must negotiate its own disappearance. Israel must decide whether each weapon surrendered is enough to pause the next strike. The Americans must turn those two incompatible jobs into a working group.

Inside Gaza, the practical question remains: who will hold the keys to the arms depots while everyone waits to see whether the war is truly over?

📡 Gharibabadi rebukes trump over strait of Hormuz claim

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs Kazem Gharibabadi has rejected a claim by US President Donald Trump that the Strait of Hormuz is part of US territory, saying Tehran will correct Trump’s “delusions.”

Gharibabadi responded on X to an image reposted by Trump describing the Strait of Hormuz as a “new part of US territory.”
​
“As Trump correctly wrote the name of the ever-Persian Gulf, soon his delusion regarding the Strait of Hormuz will either be corrected, or we will correct the delusions of this delusional person,” Gharibabadi wrote.
​
The remarks came after Trump published the image portraying the strategic waterway as part of US territory.

Trump Is Gambling With World War III By Threatening To Destroy Oman 🇴🇲


Trump has again threatened to bomb Oman if it “gets in the way” of his effort to end the US-Israel war on Iran, as the two-month window to negotiate peace with Iran expired on Monday with no end to the conflict in sight.

The latest threats against Oman, which is not a party to the war, have illustrated how Trump’s unpredictable and often outrageous approach to diplomacy has upset US partners and failed to achieve the breakthrough that he has promised to end the war.

“If Oman gets in the way, we’ll bomb the shit out of them,”
 Trump told Fox News on Monday, the second time he has directed such a threat at Muscat, a longtime US strategic partner that has traditionally served as a key backchannel between Washington and Tehran.

The various conflicts in the Middle East continued on Monday, with Yemen’s Houthis claiming to have targeted military ships from Saudi Arabia – a US ally – in a missile and drone strike in the Red Sea. Saudi officials did not confirm the strike, which the Houthis said had struck a Saudi military ship and four escort vessels. The attack is said to have taken place at a port close to the Bab-al Mandeb strait, an important global shipping route that connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.

In Israel, Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner met Benjamin Netanyahu for more than four hours after the Israeli prime minister rejected a US-backed peace plan for the Gaza war that included a withdrawal of Israeli troops from the devastated territory.

Netanyahu has said he rejected any withdrawal that would take place before Hamas fully disarms. Kushner was said to have told Netanyahu not to create obstacles to a peace deal, US officials told media outlets.

Trump has staked the political legacy of his second presidential term as being the “peacemaker-in-chief”, but his efforts to disengage the US from conflicts across the Middle East are stalling.

The US president delivered the threat against Oman as he struggles to draw the conflict to a conclusion, almost six months after it was launched, and as a diplomatic window agreed with Tehran ran out with no final agreement in sight. But Trump also claimed during Monday’s interview that he was “not in a hurry” to reach a deal.

That two-month window for a negotiated settlement closed on Monday without a breakthrough. Trump has repeatedly claimed the war would end “soon”, and talked up the prospect of a lasting peace deal in recent months, without such a breakthrough materialising.

The strait of Hormuz – a crucial chokepoint for global trade, through which about a fifth of the world’s seaborne oil supplies typically pass – has been all but closed since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran in February.

In addition to Oman’s decades-long military and economic ties with the US, the Gulf nation of 5.3 million people has played a mediation role in the war and has itself come under attack from Tehran.

Iran’s foreign ministry said on Monday that talks with Oman were “continuing in earnest”, despite Trump’s latest outburst.

Trump also confirmed for the first time that Washington had opened a direct backchannel to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), which the US and Israel have targeted throughout the conflict.

“They’re good poker players, but they’re dying,” 
he said of the IRGC leadership.
